sources.name: Knill, Fermionic Linear Optics and Matchgates
Jozsa and Miyake, Matchgates and classical simulation

model.sector: the selected two-level pendulum subspace on an open M-cell chain
model.hamiltonian: H=Delta sum_j n_j+t sum_j(a_j^dagger a_{j+1}+a_{j+1}^dagger a_j)
model.mapping: the nearest-neighbour hard-core chain maps by Jordan-Wigner to number-conserving free fermions; in the one-excitation sector this is the open path adjacency problem

logicalCompiler.assumption: arbitrary-pair logical fermionic Givens rotations; hardware routing and synthesis precision are excluded
logicalCompiler.pendulumBasisInputOutput: 144M local Givens rotations from the 72-Givens per-cell transform in Wave 7.166

commissioning.prediction: site-resolved amplitudes and phases must equal S diag(exp(-iT epsilon_k)) S^T applied to the prepared state
commissioning.nullUse: the exactly soluble evolution is a baseline for separating ordinary free propagation, basis leakage, disorder and edge effects from any later Monster-specific claim
commissioning.failureMeaning: disagreement beyond calibrated preparation, synthesis and measurement errors falsifies the implemented selected-subspace hopping model; it is not evidence for moonshine by itself

established: the ideal selected-exchange stress lane has an exact number-conserving free-fermion/matchgate compilation with zero product-formula error and an explicit O(M^2) logical resource upper bound
boundary: This result is exact only for the ideal selected two-level nearest-neighbour chain. It neither realizes the Leech lattice nor the Monster, and it excludes multilevel leakage, finite-precision gate synthesis, connectivity routing, disorder and hardware noise. Matchgate simulability makes it a calibration null model, not a quantum-advantage or new-physics result.
